title: Localized Segal-presheaf presentations of algebroids
statement:
Use [def-coef-complete-algebroid], [def-coef-segal-presheaf-localization] and [lem-coef-cocomplete-monoidal-tensor]. For small monoidal $C$, $P(C)$ with Day convolution is presentably monoidal. The presheaf category $P(C_\otimes)$ is presentable and has pointwise small colimits. Spaces admit small colimits and cartesian product of spaces preserves them separately. The full subcategory $Q_C$ is the presentable reflective localization at the labelled spine maps. For a monoidally compatible small set $S$, $P^S(C)$ is a monoidal reflective localization of $P(C)$ with strong monoidal reflector and lax monoidal fully faithful right adjoint. The category $Q_C^S$ is the presentable reflective localization of $Q_C$ at $L_CE_C(\phi)\to L_CE_C(\psi)$ for $(\phi\to\psi)\in S$.
There are natural equivalences
$$\operatorname{Algd}(P(C))\simeq Q_C,\qquad\operatorname{Algd}(P^S(C))\simeq Q_C^S.$$
The first identifies the object space of an algebroid $A$ with $Z([0])$ and its mapping object $A(x,y)\in P(C)$ with $H_Z(x,y)$. For every $Z\in Q_C$ there is a natural equivalence of spaces over $Z([0])^2$
$$\operatorname{Map}_{P(C_\otimes)}(E_C(\phi),Z)\simeq\int_{(x,y)\in Z([0])^2}\operatorname{Map}_{P(C)}(\phi,H_Z(x,y)),$$
where the integral denotes the total space of the indicated family. Consequently $Z\in Q_C^S$ exactly when every $H_Z(x,y)$ is $S$-local; the second equivalence is the restriction of the first to these objects. The reflector $L_C^S$ keeps the object space and applies the coefficient reflector to each mapping object.
Every presentably monoidal infinity category $V$ has a strong monoidal presentation $V\simeq P^S(C)$ for small monoidal $C$ and monoidally compatible small $S$. For presentations $V\simeq P^S(C)$ and $W\simeq P^T(D)$, $S\odot T$ is monoidally compatible and
$$V\otimes_{\mathrm{coc}}W\simeq P^{S\odot T}(C\times D).$$
Under the displayed algebroid equivalences, the bifunctor $\mu_*(A\boxtimes B)$ corresponds to
$$H(X,Y)=L_{C\times D}^{S\odot T}(i_C^SX\boxtimes i_D^TY).$$
For $S=T=\varnothing$, it corresponds to the external product of Segal presheaves itself. All these identifications are natural in coherent diagrams and on their canonical maps.

source.place: Observation 4.9; Proposition 5.1 and Corollary 5.8; Proposition 8.2, Lemma 8.3, Observation 8.4; fibrewise correction of Proposition 8.5 and Observations 8.6-8.7, detailed in report.md; Higher Topos Theory section 5.1.2 (pointwise presheaf colimits). Agent reconstruction of the corrected localization model; no Stacks tag states it.

proof.text: By [lem-coef-infinity-presheaf-presentability], applied to the small quasicategories $C$ and $C_\otimes$ (the total category $C_\otimes$ is small because $C$ is) and to $D=\Delta^0$, where evaluation at the unique vertex identifies $P(\Delta^0)$ with spaces, the categories $P(C)$, $P(C_\otimes)$ and spaces are presentable. By [lem-coef-space-presheaf-cocompletion], $X\times-$ has the right adjoint $\operatorname{Map}(X,-)$. For a small diagram $(Y_i)$ with colimit $Y$ and any space $Z$, $\operatorname{Map}(X\times Y,Z)\simeq\operatorname{Map}(Y,\operatorname{Map}(X,Z))\simeq\lim_i\operatorname{Map}(Y_i,\operatorname{Map}(X,Z))\simeq\lim_i\operatorname{Map}(X\times Y_i,Z)$, so by the cocone criterion of [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits] cartesian product with a fixed space preserves small colimits, in each variable by symmetry. By [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits], presheaf colimits are computed pointwise. The Day tensor of [lem-coef-operadic-day-convolution] is separately cocontinuous, hence $P(C)$ is presentably monoidal. These assertions include empty colimits.

The labelled spines in [def-coef-segal-presheaf-localization] form a small set of arrows: their labels range over finite lists in the small category $C$. Mapping a spine pushout into $Z$ gives the iterated pullback of edge values over vertex values, by [lem-coef-space-yoneda-density] and the colimit-to-limit formula of [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits]. Thus locality for exactly these arrows is exactly the displayed Segal condition, not an extra completeness condition. Apply [lem-coef-presentable-infinity-adjoints] to obtain the presentable reflective category $Q_C$ and its reflector $L_C$.

source.place: Section 4, Segal presheaves and their spine localization

proof.text: For the coefficient category let $q:P(C)\to P^S(C)$ be the small-set reflector furnished by [lem-coef-presentable-infinity-adjoints]. Monoidal compatibility is precisely the condition on tensoring the generators in [def-coef-segal-presheaf-localization]. By [lem-coef-infinity-small-localization-saturation] its inverted arrows are the strongly saturated closure of $S$. For [lem-coef-infinity-reflector-accessibility], use the same small test set $S$: every $S$-local object lies in the right-adjoint image and, by adjunction, tests every $q$-inverted arrow as an equivalence. That criterion makes $rq$ accessible. The generator criterion of [lem-coef-associative-reflective-localization] therefore applies: it makes $q$ strong monoidal and its fully faithful right adjoint $r$ lax monoidal. Only the coefficient category is asserted monoidal here; no internal tensor structure on $Q_C$ is required.

Fix a small Kan space $X$ and the left-fibration model $\Delta_X^{\mathrm{op}}$ of [def-coef-complete-algebroid]. By [lem-coef-tuple-operad-incidence], this is a generalized nonsymmetric infinity operad: its degree-zero fibre is $X$, its inert lifts are cocartesian, its Segal maps are equivalences (including $n=0$), and its vertex-edge incidence maps are equivalences, also for empty $X$.

source.place: Section 5, universal property before Proposition 5.1; explicit tuple-operad check

proof.text:
Apply [lem-coef-operadic-day-convolution] to this operad. An algebra $A$ is therefore a multiplicative space-valued functor $M$ on $\Delta_X^{\mathrm{op}}\times_{\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}}C^{\mathrm{op},\otimes}$, with $M(x_0,\ldots,x_n;\boldsymbol c)=\prod_iA(x_{i-1},x_i)(c_i)$. Pulling the tuple left fibration back to $C_\otimes^{\mathrm{op}}$ and applying [lem-coef-left-fibration-dependent-sum] to the unstraightening of $M$ gives a coherent presheaf
$$N(A)([n](\boldsymbol c))=\int_{X^{n+1}}\prod_iA(x_{i-1},x_i)(c_i).$$
Its transports are those of $M$; active maps use the algebra operations and inert maps select sublists. Its vertex value is $X$, since the nullary product is a point. Its edge fibres are $A(x,y)$; the products give the Segal equivalences of [def-coef-segal-presheaf-localization].

source.place: Section 5, universal property before Proposition 5.1; explicit construction from fibre families

proof.text: Conversely, for $Z\in Q_C$ put $X=Z([0])$ and pull $Z([n](\boldsymbol c))$ back along each tuple in $X^{n+1}$. The Segal maps identify this fibre with $\prod_iH_Z(x_{i-1},x_i)(c_i)$. By [lem-coef-left-fibration-dependent-sum] and [lem-coef-space-transport-classification] these fibres and their coherent transports assemble to the multiplicative functor $M$; the active maps induced by $Z$ give its operations. Then [lem-coef-operadic-day-convolution] recovers an algebra $A_Z$.

source.place: Section 5, universal property before Proposition 5.1; reconstruction from Segal fibres

proof.text: The constructions of steps 5–6 are inverse: on each colour the reconstructed presheaf is $A(x,y)$, with every operation the original operation, by the evaluation and naturality clauses of [lem-coef-operadic-day-convolution]. In the other direction the maps $N(A_Z)([n](\boldsymbol c))\to Z([n](\boldsymbol c))$ are over the identity of $X^{n+1}$ and induce the Segal fibre equivalences. They are equivalences by [lem-coef-spaces-homotopy-fiber-detection]. The pointwise-equivalence criterion of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] makes the comparison an equivalence of coherent presheaves. These maps assemble on every arrow by their construction through the straightening equivalence [lem-coef-space-transport-classification]. Its mapping-space comparison and the Day equivalence show the same inverses on transformations and their higher simplices. Allowing a map of spaces $X\to X'$ uses pullback of families and the corresponding operad map $\Delta_X^{\mathrm{op}}\to\Delta_{X'}^{\mathrm{op}}$; both cited equivalences commute with these. This proves the equivalence of total variable-object categories $\operatorname{Algd}(P(C))\simeq Q_C$, with the asserted identifications of objects and homs.

source.place: Propositions 5.1 and 5.3, reconstructed on fibres and transformations

proof.text:
Write $X=Z([0])$, and $Z_1(c)=Z([1](c))$ viewed over the constant presheaf $X^2$. For the fibre inclusion $u:C\to C_\otimes$, extend $c\mapsto y(u(c))$ cocontinuously using [lem-coef-infinity-presheaf-free-cocompletion]. On a representable $y(c)$, Yoneda gives $\operatorname{Map}(y(u(c)),Z)\simeq Z_1(c)\simeq\operatorname{Map}(y(c),Z_1)$. Express $\phi$ as a small colimit of representables by [lem-coef-space-yoneda-density]; mapping out of that colimit converts both sides to the same limit by [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits]. Thus the extension is left adjoint to restriction, hence is $J_C$, and $\operatorname{Map}(J_C\phi,Z)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{P(C)}(\phi,Z_1)$. Mapping the defining pushout for $E_C\phi$ in [def-coef-segal-presheaf-localization] into $Z$, using [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits] and [lem-coef-space-yoneda-density], gives
$$\operatorname{Map}(E_C\phi,Z)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{P(C)}(\phi,Z_1)\times_{\operatorname{Map}_{P(C)}(\phi,\operatorname{const}X^2)}X^2.$$
Indeed the shared-boundary term is $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal S}(a_\phi,X^2)$, which is the middle denominator by the defining colimit adjunction for $a_\phi$. The map from $X^2$ sends an endpoint pair to its constant boundary map. The homotopy fibre of this pullback over $(x,y)$ is $\operatorname{Map}_{P(C)}(\phi,H_Z(x,y))$, since mapping into a homotopy fibre preserves that limit by the cited mapping-space limit formula. The family/total-space equivalence of [lem-coef-left-fibration-dependent-sum] now gives exactly the asserted equivalence over $X^2$, natural in $\phi$ and $Z$. In particular $\phi=\varnothing$ gives $X^2$, as required by $E_C(\varnothing)=v\amalg v$.

source.place: Corrected Observations 8.6–8.7: fixed endpoints rather than raw fibrewise left Kan extension

proof.text: For $s:\phi\to\psi$ the map of step 8 is over the identity of $X^2$; its fibre is $\operatorname{Map}(\psi,H_Z(x,y))\to\operatorname{Map}(\phi,H_Z(x,y))$. Thus [lem-coef-spaces-homotopy-fiber-detection] says that $Z$ is local for $E_C(s)$ if and only if each hom fibre is $S$-local. The set of $L_C E_C(s)$ is small. Since $Q_C$ is presentable, [lem-coef-presentable-infinity-adjoints] constructs its reflective localization at this set. The adjunction $L_C\dashv i_C$ identifies its tests with the tests by $E_C(s)$ in presheaves, so its full local subcategory is exactly $Q_C^S$ of [def-coef-segal-presheaf-localization]. This proves the claimed presentability and universal property, including when $X$ or some fibres are empty.

For each small object space $X$, apply the algebra-adjunction clause of [lem-coef-associative-reflective-localization] to $\mathcal O=\Delta_X^{\mathrm{op}}$ and to $q\dashv r$ from step 3. It gives $q_*\dashv r_*$ on algebras with this fixed object space. This assembles to the variable-object adjunction as follows. By [def-coef-complete-algebroid], a morphism from $(X,A)$ to $(Y,B)$ is a map $f:X\to Y$ together with a transformation $A\to f^*B$. For each such $f$, the fixed-operad adjunction identifies transformations $q_*A\to f^*B$ with transformations $A\to r_*f^*B$. Composition with coefficient functors commutes with precomposition, so $r_*f^*B=f^*r_*B$; naturality under operad restriction in the cited clause makes these equivalences coherent over the space of all $f$. The fibrewise equivalences induce an equivalence on total mapping spaces by [lem-coef-spaces-homotopy-fiber-detection], with the identity on the base $\operatorname{Map}(X,Y)$; hence they give $q_*\dashv r_*$ on algebroids, and both functors leave the object space fixed. The coefficient counit is an equivalence, hence its composite with every algebra is an equivalence, so $r_*$ is fully faithful. The full-sub-operad clause of [lem-coef-associative-reflective-localization] identifies its image exactly with algebras whose hom objects are local. Steps 7 and 9 identify this full subcategory with $Q_C^S$, restricting the first equivalence to $\operatorname{Algd}(P^S(C))\simeq Q_C^S$. Transporting the adjunction gives a left adjoint to $Q_C^S\subset Q_C$; its mapping-space universal property identifies it with the reflector in step 9, including the unit. Thus $L_C^S$ fixes the object space and coefficient-reflects each hom.

For a presentably monoidal $\mathcal V$ choose the tensor-closed small category $C$ of $\kappa$-compact objects provided by [lem-coef-monoidal-compact-generators], with strong monoidal dense inclusion $j$. The Yoneda extension theorem in [lem-coef-operadic-day-convolution] supplies a colimit-preserving strong monoidal $q:P(C)\to\mathcal V$ whose right adjoint is restricted Yoneda $R$. This $R$ is fully faithful and preserves $\kappa$-filtered colimits by the compact density theorem. Consequently $Rq$ is accessible: $q$ preserves all colimits and $R$ preserves these filtered colimits. By [lem-coef-accessible-localization-small-generators], $q$ is generated by a small set $S$ and $\mathcal V\simeq P^S(C)$. Since $q$ is strong monoidal, tensoring any generator with any presheaf on either side is still inverted by $q$; hence $S$ is monoidally compatible by [def-coef-segal-presheaf-localization]. The monoidal localization property of [lem-coef-associative-reflective-localization] identifies the descended monoidal structure with that of $\mathcal V$.

source.place: Proposition 8.2; Chu–Haugseng Proposition 7.15 and proof of Corollary 7.16

proof.text: By [lem-coef-infinity-presheaf-free-cocompletion], extending along Yoneda one variable at a time identifies separately cocontinuous bifunctors $P(C)\times P(D)\to\mathcal E$ with cocontinuous functors $P(C\times D)\to\mathcal E$, including transformations. Under this equivalence $(p,q)$ is $p\boxtimes q$: it is separately cocontinuous by step 1 and sends $(y(c),y(d))$ to $y(c,d)$. By [lem-coef-space-yoneda-density], expressing the other argument as a small colimit of representables shows that inverting $s\boxtimes y(d)$ and $y(c)\boxtimes t$ is equivalent to inverting the coefficient generators in either variable with the other argument arbitrary. Apply [lem-coef-cocontinuous-localization-factorization] first in one variable and then in the other. It identifies such bifunctors exactly with the separately cocontinuous bifunctors $P^S(C)\times P^T(D)\to\mathcal E$. The equivalence includes transformations, so the second descent retains cocontinuity in the first variable.

source.place: Lemma 8.3, expanded using free cocompletion and localizations

proof.text: The small set $S\odot T$ in [def-coef-segal-presheaf-localization] consists exactly of those generator maps. Apply [lem-coef-cocontinuous-localization-factorization] to the presentable category $P(C\times D)$ and this set. By step 12, cocontinuous functors from its localization to each locally small cocomplete $\mathcal E$ are therefore exactly the separately cocontinuous bifunctors on $\mathcal V\times\mathcal W$. This is the universal property in [lem-coef-cocomplete-monoidal-tensor], proving $\mathcal V\otimes_{\mathrm{coc}}\mathcal W\simeq P^{S\odot T}(C\times D)$. The universal bifunctor sends the localized pair $(p,q)$ to $q_{S\odot T}(r_Sp\boxtimes r_Tq)$: the factorization of the external product is its restriction along the two fully faithful right adjoints. The unit and counit comparisons in the factorization lemma identify its canonical maps and transformations.

source.place: Lemma 8.3, expanded using free cocompletion and localizations

proof.text: Restore monoidal structures. On representables the functor $(c,d)\mapsto\mu(q_Sy(c),q_Ty(d))$ is strong monoidal, by [lem-coef-cocomplete-monoidal-tensor] and the strong monoidal reflectors from step 3. Extend by [lem-coef-operadic-day-convolution] to a colimit-preserving strong monoidal $b:P(C\times D)\to\mathcal V\otimes_{\mathrm{coc}}\mathcal W$. By the preceding universal property, $b$ is the localization at $S\odot T$, since on all external presheaves it is $\mu(q_Sp,q_Tq)$ (both sides are separately cocontinuous extensions of the same values on representables). It inverts the generators, and because it is strong monoidal it also inverts every generator tensored on either side with any presheaf. Thus $S\odot T$ is monoidally compatible. By [lem-coef-associative-reflective-localization] the equivalence of steps 12–13 is strong monoidal and identifies the universal coefficient bifunctor with $(p,q)\mapsto q_{S\odot T}(r_Sp\boxtimes r_Tq)$.

source.place: Lemma 8.3 and its identification of the universal monoidal bifunctor

proof.text: By [lem-coef-algebroid-external-product], $A\boxtimes B$ has object space $X\times Y$ and pairs of hom objects. In the unlocalized presheaf case, step 12 identifies $\mu$ on hom objects with external cartesian product. The formula of step 5 then identifies its nerve at $[n](\boldsymbol c,\boldsymbol d)$ with $N(A)([n](\boldsymbol c))\times N(B)([n](\boldsymbol d))$: over the object tuple this is the equality between the product of the two products of hom spaces and the product of their paired hom spaces; taking total spaces commutes with this external product by the external-product clause of [lem-coef-left-fibration-dependent-sum]. This also identifies operations, since they are the paired operations. Thus the unlocalized model is exactly the external Segal presheaf. In the localized case apply the lax right adjoints to $A,B$, use this same construction, and apply $q_{S\odot T,*}$. Step 14 identifies its coefficient functor with $\mu$, and step 10 identifies its nerve with $L_{C\times D}^{S\odot T}(i_C^S N(A)\boxtimes i_D^T N(B))$. This is the claimed $H$. Naturality on all coherent diagrams and canonical maps follows at the level of functors: the Day equivalence is natural in operads and coefficient functors by [lem-coef-operadic-day-convolution], straightening is natural on transformations and pullbacks by [lem-coef-space-transport-classification], and the unit/counit factorization argument in steps 12–13 identifies the localization equivalences on transformations as well as objects. In particular the transported localization maps are the units already identified in step 10, rather than unspecified isomorphisms of objects.
